# A method's ambient `this` and a `ref<T>` parameter are passed by reference,
# and a named parameter is a value, on every target: testdata/ref_params.sngl
# is the program, and testdata/ref_params.txtar the code.

sngl test --platform=none app.sngl
stdout '4 tests, 0 failures'

sngl test --platform=html app.sngl
stdout '4 tests, 0 failures'

sngl test --platform=bubbletea --language=go app.sngl
stdout '4 tests, 0 failures'

sngl test --platform=fyne --language=go app.sngl
stdout '4 tests, 0 failures'

sngl test --platform=gtk4 --language=go app.sngl
stdout '4 tests, 0 failures'

sngl test --platform=android --language=kotlin app.sngl
stdout '4 tests, 0 failures'

-- app.sngl --
// A call passes two parameters by reference: a method's ambient `this`, the
// receiver's own value, and a parameter declared `ref<T>`, the cell `&x`
// hands it. A named parameter of any other type is a value. A function
// writing one by reference hands back what it wrote and the call writes it to
// the place it passed (passRefParams), so the program reads the same on every
// target.

import . "sngl:test"
import ui "sngl:ui"

struct Stack {
    items  list<int> = []
    pushes int = 0

    // The ambient `this` is the receiver's own value: a method writing it
    // writes the caller's.
    func add(x int) {
        this.items.push(x)
        this.pushes += 1
    }

    // A method handing `this` to another that writes it writes it too.
    func addTwice(x int) {
        add(x)
        add(x)
    }

    // A method that writes `this` and returns a value of its own.
    func pop() int {
        var top = this.items[this.items.length() - 1]
        this.items.remove(this.items.length() - 1)
        return top
    }

    // One that only reads `this` writes nothing back.
    func size() => this.items.length()
}

// A named parameter is a value; `ref<T>` is the caller's cell.
func fill(s ref<Stack>) {
    s.add(7)
}

func reset(s ref<Stack>) {
    *s = Stack{}
}

func peek(s ref<Stack>) int {
    return s.items.length()
}

// A whole value is written through a reference with `*`.
func setTo(x ref<int>, v int) {
    *x = v
}

func touch(s Stack) int {
    s.add(1)
    return s.items.length()
}

component box ui.node {
    var (
        st = Stack{}
        all list<Stack> = [Stack{}, Stack{}]
        k = 0
        out = ""
    )

    func methods() {
        st.add(1)
        st.addTwice(2)
        var top = st.pop()
        out = "{st.items.length()} {st.pushes} {top} {st.size()}"
    }

    func refs() {
        fill(&st)
        var n = peek(&st)
        setTo(&k, 4)
        reset(&all[1])
        all[0].add(3)
        for var &s = all {
            s.add(5)
        }
        out = "{st.items.length()} {n} {k} {all[0].items.length()} {all[1].items.length()}"
    }

    func values() {
        var n = touch(st)
        out = "{st.items.length()} {n}"
    }

    ui.text #o(value=out)
}

func testThisIsTheReceiver(t Test, c box) {
    c.methods()
    t.assert(c.o.value == "2 3 2 2")
}

func testRefParamIsTheCallersCell(t Test, c box) {
    c.refs()
    t.assert(c.o.value == "1 1 4 2 1")
}

func testNamedParamIsAValue(t Test, c box) {
    c.values()
    t.assert(c.o.value == "0 1")
}

func testATestCallsAMethod(t Test, c box) {
    c.st.add(9)
    t.assert(c.st.items.length() == 1)
}

ui.window {
    box
}
